snippet.title: Tax on Spain Digital Nomad Visa for Pakistani Passport Holders
snippet.description:
Are you a Pakistani passport holder applying for the Spain Digital Nomad Visa and confused about taxes? In this video, I explain how tax works for Spain Digital Nomad Visa holders, especially for Pakistani applicants working remotely for foreign companies or clients.

Many people think that getting the Spain Digital Nomad Visa automatically means paying only 24% tax, but that is not always the case. Your tax situation depends on whether you become a tax resident in Spain, whether you qualify for the special tax regime, your source of income, and your personal circumstances.

In this video, we cover:

✅ Do Pakistani passport holders pay tax in Spain on the Digital Nomad Visa?
✅ What happens if you stay in Spain for more than 183 days?
✅ Difference between visa residence and tax residence
✅ What is the 24% special tax regime / Beckham Law?
✅ Can remote workers and digital nomads apply for the special tax regime?
✅ Spain and Pakistan double taxation treaty explained simply
✅ Common tax mistakes Digital Nomad Visa applicants make
✅ Why you should speak to a tax advisor before moving to Spain

This video is useful for Pakistani freelancers, remote workers, business owners, IT professionals, consultants, and employees planning to move to Spain under the Digital Nomad Visa.

snippet.title: Camino de la Ría de Muros y Noia: A Brand New Way
snippet.description:
The Camino de la Ría de Muros y Noia starts in Muros and follows a wishbone shape along the Galician coast before heading inland to Santiago de Compostela. This newly marked route gets to the heart of Galicia. Walk it now before it gets discovered!

The Camino de la Ría de Muros y Noia follows the route used my mariners and crusaders in the Middle Ages.

Here's the awesome smartwatch that made our GPS maps: https://suunto.pxf.io/zzzR6e 

We started our walk on February 27, 2026 in Muros, Spain, and walked the 102 km route in 5 days. 

This is our 15th Camino together. In 2025, we walked the Camino de Santiago de Gran Canaria, the Camino Inglés, and the Camiño Dos Faros. In 2024, we walked the Camino Sanabrés, Camino Lebaniego, Camino Vadiniense, Camino San Salvador, and Camino de Madrid. We hiked the Camino Frances, Via Podiensis, Camino Primitivo, and Camino de Invierno in 2023. We walked the Camino del Norte in 2019 and the Camino Frances in 2017. Yes, Da Nang is a popular destination for digital nomads due to its affordable cost of living, reliable internet, and growing coworking spaces.

You can live comfortably in Da Nang for around $1000/month, including accommodation, food, transportation, and entertainment.

Popular neighborhoods include My Khe Beach (for beach lovers), Hai Chau District (city center), and Son Tra Peninsula (quiet and scenic).

Yes, most travelers need a visa. Vietnam offers a 90-day e-visa for multiple entries, and some nationalities enjoy visa exemptions for up to 45 days.

Da Nang is considered very safe for expats, with low crime rates and a friendly local population.

Da Nang has a tropical climate with a dry season (February to May) and a rainy season (September to December).

FAQs:
1. Is Da Nang a good place for digital nomads?
Yes, Da Nang is a popular destination for digital nomads due to its affordable cost of living, reliable internet, and growing coworking spaces.

2. How much does it cost to live in Da Nang?
You can live comfortably in Da Nang for around $1000/month, including accommodation, food, transportation, and entertainment.

3. What is the best area to live in Da Nang?
Popular neighborhoods include My Khe Beach (for beach lovers), Hai Chau District (city center), and Son Tra Peninsula (quiet and scenic).

4. Do I need a visa to live in Da Nang?
Yes, most travelers need a visa. Vietnam offers a 90-day e-visa for multiple entries, and some nationalities enjoy visa exemptions for up to 45 days.

5. Is Da Nang safe for expats?
Da Nang is considered very safe for expats, with low crime rates and a friendly local population.

6.What is the internet speed like in Da Nang?
Internet speeds in Da Nang are reliable, with many coworking spaces and cafes offering high-speed connections suitable for remote work.

7. What are the best coworking spaces in Da Nang?
Top coworking spaces include Enouvo Space, DNC Coworking Space, and Space A.

8.Can I rent a motorbike in Da Nang?
Yes, motorbike rentals are widely available and cost around $50-$70/month, making it the most popular way to get around.

9. What is the food like in Da Nang?
Da Nang is a food lover’s paradise, offering delicious street food like Mi Quang and Banh Xeo, as well as affordable local and Western restaurants.

10. What are the must-visit attractions in Da Nang?
Don’t miss the Dragon Bridge, Marble Mountains, Linh Ung Pagoda, and a day trip to Hoi An Ancient Town.

11. How is healthcare in Da Nang?
Healthcare in Da Nang is improving, with private hospitals like Vinmec and Family Medical Practice offering high-quality care. Expats are advised to have international health insurance.

12. What is the weather like in Da Nang?
Da Nang has a tropical climate with a dry season (February to May) and a rainy season (September to December).

13. Can I live in Da Nang on $500/month?
While possible, living on $500/month would require strict budgeting. $1000/month allows for a more comfortable lifestyle.

14. Is Da Nang cheaper than Ho Chi Minh City?
Yes, Da Nang is generally cheaper than Ho Chi Minh City, especially for accommodation and dining.

15. What is the best time to visit Da Nang?
The best time to visit Da Nang is during the dry season (February to May) when the weather is sunny and pleasan

Comparte experiencia, conocimiento técnico, análisis estratégico y responsabilidad legal.

La realidad incómoda es que muchas denegaciones no ocurren por culpa del trámite.

Ocurren porque nadie diseñó correctamente la estrategia antes de presentar el expediente.

Por eso en Lexborders insistimos en algo que repetimos constantemente:

Lexborders no tramita papeles; diseña estrategia legal antes de que el error ocurra.
